newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS- Jump on BTP bandwagon while it lasts.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS- Jump on BTP bandwagon while it lasts.

text.p: To stand in the way of Italian bonds is like lying in the path of a freight train these days, analysts said on Tuesday.
This week's show of optimism from European finance ministers on Italy joining a single currency in the first wave pushed the yield spread between the BTPs and Bunds from triple into double digits.
With investors still gung-ho on European economic and monetary union (EMU) starting on time, the 10-year spread could easily reach 75 basis points over the coming weeks from 96 now, analysts said.
"With the kind of momentum we're seeing in bond convergence, we could see the spread touching 75 very quickly," said David Brown, chief economist at Bear Stearns International in London.
Investors would "scrape the bottom of the barrel" in terms of spread convergence trades while signs of a soft EMU continued to boost Italy's prospects, he said.
Robert Prior, European economist at HSBC James Capel agreed. "I can't see anything that's going to stop the BTP convergence trades in the short-term," he said.
In a record-breaking streak September BTP futures have gained nearly six percent in the last month. By 1130 GMT, the contract was 0.11 down on the day at 136.13.
The spread against Bunds had shrunk from around 150 basis points in early June.
Rome won qualified approval from the European Union (EU) on Monday for its efforts to get its finances into shape for currency union.

In a statement in Brussels, European finance ministers "acknowledged with satisfaction the remarkable progress in convergence achieved by Italy, particularly as regards inflation, interest rates and currency stability".
But they said Italy must streamline its pensions scheme in line with economic growth.

In a convergence plan, Italy forecast its budget deficit would be bang on the EMU target of three precent of GDP for 1997, and at 2.8 pct for 1998. But short-term, political snags could still derail bond convergence. "The risk is that EMU is not a done deal," said Brown of Bear Stearns.

Brian Venables, senior bond strategist at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Amsterdam, said the spread would pause at 100 before taking another plunge towards 80, possibly by September. "We've now had the talk, let's have the action," said Venables, referring to Rome's EMU promises.
But summer holidays in Italy were likely to stall the political momentum until the beginning of September.
Political reaction in the German regions towards a soft EMU route, and wrangling between France and Germany over the powers of the European Central Bank (ECB) could also disrupt bond convergence.
"Not only could we see 150 taken out in the next three to six months, but we could also reach 200 levels," said Brown.
One threat for Italy was the debt/GDP ratio which was currently well above the 60 percent EMU requirement at around 125 percent.
Prior said the BTP spread was unlikely to overtake Bonos. The Bonos/Bund spread is currently at 68 basis points.
"70-80 would be about as far as it would go," he said adding that convergence would unwind by the end of the year as he expected EMU to be delayed.
